paragraphs.text: While Jeroboam did evil as he could, walking contrary to God, God also walked as contrary to him; for is it fit that he should lay down the bucklers first
His son and heir, likely, as was also Rehoboam’s son Abijah, not Abiud, as Sulpitius Severus calleth him.

To her, rather than to another messenger, for secrecy’s sake; for although he knew that his son’s sickness was sent of God, yet he was loath openly to seek help of him, lest people should think the worse of his idols, as not able to relieve him; or by his example, run to God’s true prophets in their distress. Whether Jeroboam’s wife was sister to the queen of Egypt, and called by the name of Ano, as the Septuagint say, or Anna, as some others, is not very material.
paragraphs.anchor: And Jeroboam said to his wife.

paragraphs.text: Either there he dwelt, or thither he had retired himself, as irked at the king’s idolatries.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, there is Abijah the prophet.

paragraphs.text: Therein he told truth; and therefore also he will in this case.
paragraphs.anchor: Which told me that I should be king.

paragraphs.text: A poor country present, that she might seem none other than a plain country woman, yet willing to show her thankfulness.
paragraphs.anchor: And take with thee ten loaves.

paragraphs.text: Or, Plain cakes; Heb., Punctata, tenues placentulas punctis respersas.

Or, Bottle, a narrow mouthed vessel, that when it is emptied soundeth bakbuk, that is the Hebrew word here used. See the like in Job 39:30, where the vultures are said to glut glut blood, by an onomatopoeia.

And Jeroboam’s wife did so.] Putting off her royal attire, and putting on more demure apparel; like as many hypocrites do, conforming themselves to the company they come into, and walking in a disguise, till God detect them.
These things, therefore, were done toward the end of Jeroboam’s reign.
paragraphs.anchor: For his eyes were set by reason of his age.

paragraphs.text: Ut ipsa agit extraneam. She would have deceived the prophet, if she could; so would hypocrites deceive God of heaven, if they knew how. But he is too wise to be cajoled or cheated.
paragraphs.anchor: She shall feign herself to be another woman.

paragraphs.text: How God laughs in heaven at the frivolous fetches of crafty politicians and double-minded dissemblers! Surely when they think themselves most sure, he shameth them with a defeat. What an idleness is it for foolish hypocrites to hope that they can dance: in a net unseen of Heaven!
paragraphs.anchor: Come in, thou wife of Jeroboam.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Hard. Jeroboam was hard-hearted and refractory: a hard and heavy message is therefore sent unto him, that a hard knot may have a hard wedge. Neither is the voice of God’s word ever any better to the guilty, if impenitent. It is as the knuckles of a man’s hand were to Belshazzar, to write them their destiny, or as Daniel was to him, to read it unto them.
paragraphs.anchor: For I am sent to thee with heavy tidings.

paragraphs.text: God upbraideth not any unless it be in case of extreme ingratitude; as here, with Jas 1:5. Qui exprobat reposcit.
Antecessorem, a leader to others, a loade-star upon whom all should fix their eyes, and shape their course.
Did all my wills, {Act 13:22} in desire and endeavour at least; repenting heartily for his involuntary and unavoidable infirmities, which therefore were not imputed unto him.
viz., In mine account and acceptation.
paragraphs.anchor: To do that only which was right

paragraphs.text: Not Saul and Solomon only, but the kings of the heathens also, - as Tostatus maketh the sense, - because they knew no better: but he fell with eyes open.
paragraphs.anchor: But hast done evil above all that were before thee.

paragraphs.text: Hast laid me aside and set light by me, quasi non satis essem ad ulciscendas iniurias, as if I were nobody with thee, nor had power to punish thee. Thou hast both despised and despited me. See on Psa 50:17 Neh 9:26.
paragraphs.anchor: And hast cast me behind thy back.

paragraphs.text: Ne canibus quidem parcam; not so much as a dog of his shall escape.
paragraphs.anchor: Him that pisseth against the, wall

paragraphs.text: And him that is shut up - in some garrison - and left,] viz., To shift as they may, there being not room in the hold to receive them; as there is not for all the bees in a hive, but some are fain to hang on it at the hive’s mouth on heaps
That the pavement may be pure. Delebo omnes reliquias et quisquilias tuae familiae, I will sweep thee with the besem of destruction; and make an utter riddance of thee. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: As a man taketh away dung.

paragraphs.text: {a} Scopis everram, evertam.
A fearful judgment, such as befell Euripides the poet, and Lucian the atheist, eaten alive by dogs, as it is storied.

This heavy news could not but pierce through the mother’s soul as a sword. {Luk 2:35} A child he is called, because dearly beloved of his parents; but he was of age enough to choose the good and refuse the evil. {1Ki 14:13}
As great Britain was all in black for the loss of that hopeful Prince Henry. As Cardan sang at Edward VI’s death,
paragraphs.anchor: And all Israel shall mourn for him.

paragraphs.text: “ Flete nefas magnum, sed tote flebitis orbe
Mortales, vester corruit omnis honos.
Dignus Apollineis lacrymis doctaque Minervae
Flosculus, heu misero, concidit ante diem. ”
Briers, thorns, and thistles wither not so soon as lilies and roses. God’s darlings oft die betime: when worse men are preserved, or rather reserved, for further mischief to them.
{a} q.d., Why say I the Lord shall raise up Baasha for an executioner of his wrath? Is he not even now in doing of it? Is not Baasha busily laying his plots already for the kingdom?
{a} Quis vero si iam? - Tigur.
That never resteth, being in continual motion by wind and water, see 1Sa 25:29; the soul of a wicked man is "in a sling," violently tossed with infinite turmoils and restless.
paragraphs.anchor: As a reed is shaken in the water.

paragraphs.text: Whereunto they consented, being "carried away unto those dumb idols, even as they were led." {1Co 12:2}
paragraphs.anchor: And he shall give Israel up because of the sins of Jeroboam.

paragraphs.text: A pleasant cry, {Son 6:4} but to her at this time dismal and dolorous: the door also thereof, - whereto when she came, the child died, - like the porta Scelerata in Rome, whereof see Florus, lib. i. cap. 12.
See 1Ki 14:13.
These were annals or public records, out of which, likely, were composed the Books of Chronicles, now part of the holy Scriptures.
paragraphs.anchor: Written in the book of the chronicles.

paragraphs.text: Heb., He lay down. "This shall ye have of my hand, ye shall lie down in sorrow." {Isa 50:11} "The Lord struck Jeroboam and he died." {2Ch 13:20} He died not the common death of all men, but by some remarkable stroke: beside the loss of five hundred thousand of his men in one battle with Abijah king of Judah. {2Ch 13:17}
paragraphs.anchor: And he slept with his fathers.

paragraphs.text: His mother’s name was Naamah an Ammonitess.] Mentioned here, and again, 1Ki 14:31, but for no good. Omne malum ex Gynaeceo. She had the breeding of him, and corrupted him likely. His wicked wife also, Maachah, helped after.
Qualis rex, talis plerunque grex. Howbeit there was a remnant among the twelve tribes, thus generally revolted, that "instantly served God day and night." {Act 26:7} See 1Ki 19:10; 1Ki 19:18.
They fell to foul idolatry and sodomy, which are called evil by a specialty, {1Ki 14:22} like as war is called evil, that is, misery, antonomastice {Isa 45:7}
paragraphs.anchor: For they also built them high places.

paragraphs.text: Meritorii, male harlots, unnaturally filthy. The word here used signifieth holy ones: either by antiphrasis in a contrary meaning, or because such abomination was committed under a pretext of religion. These abandoned their bodies to suffer abominable lust. This is common in Turkey, and under the Papacy.
paragraphs.anchor: And there were also sodomites in the land.

paragraphs.text: Diodorus Siculus calleth him Sasokis; Justin, Susakis.
Drawn by a desire of Solomon’s ivory throne, say some; like as the pearls usually cast out with the flood and gathered with the ebb, drew Caesar’s affection for the conquest of Britain. {a}
{a} Sueton.

Without any great resistance; such was the pusillanimity and effeminacy of Rehoboam; which was also laid in his dish by Shishak setting up pillars and ugly pictures thereon, to the shame of the Jewish nation, as Diodorus {a} showeth.
{a} Lib. i.
"The faithful city" was now "become a harlot"; no wonder therefore that her "silver was become dross," {Isa 1:21-22} her gold brass.
Propter periculum insidiarum etiam in ipsa domo Domini metuendarum, to prevent danger.

Skirmishes there were continually about the borders.
Jeroboam lived to see three successions in the throne of Judah. Thus the ivy liveth where the oak is dead.
